HEEWON WEBTOON — bold Korean webtoon / manhwa key art, the finish of a top-tier serialised webtoon cover (Solo Leveling, Omniscient Reader, Nano Machine). A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). MEDIUM CLOSE SHOT of ONE character — waist-up or seated — the face large, placed off-centre on a third with breathing room on the side they look toward, from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye or over-the-shoulder), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. LINE: THICK, confident black ink contours with real line weight — a heavy tapered outline around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands; solid black spot-blacks fill the deepest shadows, the hair masses and the insides of sleeves. SHADING: cel-shaded in hard-edged shapes — a base tone, ONE crisp shadow shape and one small sharp highlight per surface, at most one soft gradient for form; glossy graphic highlights on hair, eyes, lacquer and steel. Clean saturated colour. NOT painterly brushwork, NOT watercolor, NOT soft sketchy lines, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. CHARACTER DESIGN: a DESIGNED character, never a generic handsome manhwa face — the face shape, eye shape, brows, nose, mouth, build and posture below belong to this person and no one else, pushed far enough that they read at thumbnail size and in silhouette alone. KOREAN FACES: these are 7th-century Koreans, drawn the way the best Korean webtoons draw Koreans — East Asian bone structure, single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, a low soft nasal bridge, broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair; varied from person to person (moon faces, long faces, square jaws), never Western, Latin or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes, never the interchangeable pretty anime face. Keep identity from the attached sheet (hair, dress, colours, ornaments) but REDRAW the person in this bolder style; the sheet's soft sketchy rendering is not the style. INTRODUCING JUMONG, the best archer in Buyeo — barely grown, about eighteen, and the princes have noticed. Morning in the princes' archery square: packed earth, a weathered timber mark-stake out of frame. Low worm's-eye three-quarter angle from beside his front foot: he is at full draw with a long wooden bow, the string at the corner of his grinning mouth, one eye half-closed down the arrow shaft, red headband tails lifting in the breeze, and he says, easy and cocky: "I'll take the fly." A boyish lopsided grin, eyes bright with mischief; completely clean-shaven, no moustache, no beard. Behind him, painted in soft morning haze: grey palace roofs, a timber palisade, dust drifting across the square, and two princes in blue and green Buyeo robes as dark out-of-focus shapes at the far edge, arms folded. The low morning sun rakes across his face, the taut bowstring and his red silk from the side in warm red-orange light (#e8563f), deep painted shadow on the far side. CHARACTER SHEET (copy this face, hair and clothes exactly): the sheet shows JUMONG. JUMONG — Look: Lean archer; black hair half-bound under a knotted red headband with long tails; dark warm eyes, easy grin. CLEAN-SHAVEN before he is king — ignore the moustache and chin hair on his portrait. Dress: Red silk jeogori and po over a charcoal underlayer, rope-tied sash, wrapped forearms; bow across his back. Colour #e8563f. DESIGN HOOKS for JUMONG: lanky and boyish: a narrow sun-browned clean-shaven face, bright single-lidded eyes crinkled almost shut with laughter, a slightly crooked nose, a huge toothy grin with one chipped front tooth, mussed half-bound coarse hair; red headband tails whipping. BACKGROUND: the real place and moment of the scene simplified into big graphic shapes — two or three flat value planes, a gradient sky or smoke, a few crisp architectural silhouettes, clean circular bokeh lights; background lines thinner and lighter than the figure so the inked character pops forward. LIGHT: ONE hard key light from the place throws a crisp cast-shadow shape across the face and lays a thin bright rim line along the silhouette; the character's colour lives in that light, never a glow aura or halo. ACTING: big readable manhwa expression and body language carrying the line they are about to say. Face and clothes from the sheet; a new pose, never the sheet's stance. ONLY THIS ONE PERSON is the subject — anyone else is at most a dark out-of-focus shape at the frame edge, in period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang or Yamato), never European dress. The quoted line is acting direction only: never letter it, no words or sound effects anywhere. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
